name: Hazard Protocol
description: Industrial and precise, made to be printed: FDM is the default process. Faces meet at chamfers and plan-view corners are rounded, so parts read angular but smooth; one chamfer angle, a short ladder of chamfer sizes and a small family of corner radii, chosen by eye and never from a ratio. Bed edges are chamfered, never filleted. Features sit on shared datums with even margins, halves meet at a shadow line on an existing edge, and the seam hides in a rear inside corner. The signature pattern is the isogrid with every pocket corner rounded at a radius equal to the rib width and no circles at the nodes, kept in a bounded zone with a solid border; Voronoi with every cell corner rounded is the alternative. Light gray bodies, dark gray structure and Hazard Orange only where something is functional, in a matte finish. Each pattern zone states its role against the wall it replaces: ribs stiffen a thin wall, a closed two-skin wall of the same depth is stiffer still, and a load rating needs evidence; where a pattern is styling, it is still part of the house look.

tokens.fastener.head: socketCap
tokens.material.preference: matte filament in the body and accent colors, where the material dfm chooses comes in them

notes.corner.radius.set: House starting family, picked by eye for hand-sized enclosures and brackets, not from a ratio; tune it per product by decision.
notes.edge.chamfer.bottom: Research starting value (dfm-research 06, sample token block, base chamfer 0.6 mm; illustrative); the DFM bed-edge floor wins when larger.
notes.edge.chamfer.sizes: House starting ladder (assumption): a small, a medium and a large chamfer; research recommends at most two sizes on outer edges of one part (dfm-research 06, A.1).
notes.edge.top.treatment: The house form language: chamfered edges where faces meet.
notes.edge.vertical.treatment: The house form language: rounded corners in plan view.
notes.fastener.head: Research sample (dfm-research 06, sample token block: socket cap screws, recessed 0.5 mm); assumption until the user rules.
notes.fastener.kinds.max: Research rule: one fastener type and size per product where possible (dfm-research 06, A.4).
notes.finish.surface: Matte hides layer lines and suits the render guide's diffuse, no-specular look (dfm-research 06, A.5; Hazard Protocol render guide, section 3).
notes.form.language: The Protoboard house look: chamfers with rounded corners, angular but smooth.
notes.layout.margin: Research sample value (dfm-research 06, sample token block, margin 4.0 mm; illustrative).
notes.manufacturing.default: House default: most designs are printed on FDM machines, so printing is the default assumption.
notes.marks.height: House starting value (assumption); the DFM floor (twice the smallest text height) wins when larger.
notes.pattern.default: The house signature pattern: the isogrid.
notes.pattern.isogrid.cell: Derived starting value for 60 to 150 mm enclosure panels (dfm-research 06, B.6: triangle height 10 to 20 mm, at least three cells across the shortest span); prove it with a printed coupon.
notes.pattern.isogrid.corner.radius.rule: House convention: pocket corner radius equals the rib (wall) width. Supported by the isogrid research: a radius at least one extrusion width keeps the toolpath smooth and lowers the stress at the rib junction (dfm-research 06, B.2).
notes.pattern.isogrid.node.circle: House convention: no circle at the nodes. The node boss is a milling artifact a printer does not have (NASA CR-124075 p. 5.0.001, via dfm-research 06, B.2); keep a boss only where something mounts.
notes.pattern.isogrid.orientation: Derived geometry (dfm-research 06, B.5): with one rib family horizontal on a vertical wall every pocket ceiling self-supports or bridges one short side.
notes.pattern.isogrid.pocket.min: Derived rule (dfm-research 06, B.2): leave a pocket solid when its inscribed radius is under two rib widths.
notes.pattern.isogrid.rib.depth: Derived starting value (dfm-research 06, B.6: 3 to 5 mm; dfm-research 09, 11.iii: depth at most about five rib widths, about 6 mm for the 1.25 mm rib); prove it with a coupon.
notes.pattern.isogrid.rib.width: Derived starting value (dfm-research 06, B.5 and B.6; dfm-research 09, 11.iii): three lines at 0.45 mm line width and 0.2 mm layers is 1.26 mm; 1.25 mm is that width rounded, which the Arachne perimeter generator prints as three beads (model 1.26 mm on the Classic generator). For parts that get handled; the DFM floor of two line widths wins when larger.
notes.pattern.isogrid.skin: Derived starting value (dfm-research 06, B.6: 1.2 mm skin, three perimeters on a vertical wall).
notes.pattern.voronoi.cell: Derived (dfm-research 06, C.2): mean cell about five to ten strut widths, opening at least about 3 mm.
notes.pattern.voronoi.corner.radius.rule: House convention: every Voronoi cell corner is rounded, at about the strut width (dfm-research 06, C.2, derived).
notes.pattern.voronoi.relaxation: Derived (dfm-research 06, C.1): 3 to 10 passes give even but organic cells; 5 is the house start.
notes.pattern.voronoi.strut: Derived (dfm-research 06, C.2): 1.2 mm or more for parts that get handled.
notes.pattern.zone.border: Derived (dfm-research 06, B.6): a solid band at least twice the rib width; 2.5 mm is twice a 1.25 mm rib.
notes.proportion.system: House convention: no ratio or proportion systems; offered only as an optional diagnostic, never applied by default.
notes.split.reveal.depth: Research recipe for printed shadow lines on 1.6 mm walls (OpenAT design guide, via dfm-research 06, A.3): lip and overlap of about this order; house starting value.
notes.split.reveal.width: House starting value (assumption); the DFM gap floor wins when larger.
notes.split.style: Research: a shadow line hides the varying gap of two printed halves and self-locates them (dfm-research 06, A.3).
notes.text.engrave.depth: Research: engraved text about four layers deep, 0.6 to 0.8 mm at 0.2 mm layers (dfm-research 06, A.4; unverified); the DFM floor wins when larger.
notes.text.height.min: Research: 4 to 6 mm cap height for reliable FDM text with a 0.4 mm nozzle (dfm-research 06, A.4; unverified community sources); 5 mm is the house start.
notes.text.stroke.min: Research: strokes of at least 0.8 to 1.0 mm (dfm-research 06, A.4; unverified).
notes.text.style: Research: raised text prints more reliably than engraved on FDM (dfm-research 06, A.4; unverified); assumption until the user rules.
